blockers.quote: One 2017 study found it tended to cool (c18). Nobody's nose is a counter.
blockers.why: Row c18 is marked contested because findings on thermal lie detection are unsettled, and claims.md explicitly instructs 'Do not state a direction (c13, c18)'. Stating that the nose tended to cool asserts a direction as fact and fails to explain why the row is contested (contradicting earlier claims of warming).
blockers.fix: Some claims say the nose warms, but one 2017 study found it tended to cool (c18)—the science is unsettled. Nobody's nose is a counter.

blockers.quote: In one US survey, almost half of all the lies came from about 5% of people (c03, c04).
blockers.why: The misconception stated in line 92 is that you are lied to 10 to 200 times a day (c12). Stating only that 5% of people tell half of all lies does not break that high-frequency belief; the key finding supported by c03 that refutes the misconception is that about 60% of people reported zero lies in the past day (verbatim quote: 'Sixty percent of subjects report telling no lies at all'). Omitting this leaves the wrong belief unbroken.
blockers.fix: In one US survey, about 60% of people reported telling no lies at all, and almost half of all the lies came from about 5% of people (c03, c04).

blockers.quote: Rival: The nose warms when you lie. I've read noses for twenty years.

blockers.fix: Rival: A liar's nose always gives them away. I've read noses for twenty years.
